correctness.rationale: There are thirteen nonzero negation pairs, giving the upper bound; the displayed word attains it. Feasible maximal words correspond bijectively to distinct labeled cyclic edge tours of complete pair selections. A balanced graph with connected active undirected support is strongly connected on that support; loops count toward degrees but cancel from the tree Laplacian. In the BEST formula one can fix a single outgoing edge at the active root, rather than multiply by the root degree. A separately written enumeration fixing the minimum chosen edge and tracing feasible unused-edge paths, without determinants or BEST, exhausted all 8192 selections and reproduced 8120 unbalanced, 12 balanced disconnected, 60 Eulerian and the full tours/degree histograms. It obtained 288 distinct rotation classes, 3744 indexed words (the distinct windows force least period 13), and 72 orbits of size four. Independently, negation cannot preserve a selected edge set. Reversal would require an index reflection of thirteen edge positions, which has only one fixed edge, whereas a full selector contains four palindromic triples. Negated reversal sends each selected palindrome to its forbidden negative. These facts also explain freeness without computation.

value.rationale: The first ternary three-window optimizer problem asks for all positional cyclic designs achieving the exact distinguishability bound, not a single witness. The counts distinguish the design space, its actual symmetries and how differently eligible balanced supports contribute. The finite cutoff is fixed by the extremal problem; it is not an arbitrary truncation or a claim of practical performance.
